writeup.headline: MSG Sports rates Hold: strong growth and price trend offset by a very high absolute valuation.
writeup.thesis: MSG Sports scores 55, a Hold with high confidence, sitting 10 points below Buy and 11 points above Sell. Growth (85) is the strongest factor, with quarterly revenue up 36.67% year on year against 11.03% on a trailing basis, and the trend factor (81) reflects a share price 14.98% above its 200-day average, 12-1 month momentum of 79.77% and only a 2.94% drawdown from its 52-week high. Valuation (12) is the main drag: in absolute terms the multiples are high, at 8.494 times sales, 159.988 times free cash flow and 342.74 times EBIT, with a free cash flow yield 4.585 points below the 10-year Treasury. Against its own history the stock is labelled expensive overall: it is "more expensive than at 53 of the last 61 month-ends" on P/S, "near the middle of the last 61 month-ends (cheaper than at 21, more expensive than at 39)" on P/FCF, and EV/EBIT is "not comparable (negative in 14 of 61 month-ends)". Quality is middling at 46, with thin margins (2.5% operating, 5.31% FCF), while the balance sheet (69) is reasonable and news risk is neutral at 50.
key_risks: Absolute valuation is high: 159.988x free cash flow and 342.74x EBIT leave little room for disappointment.
Thin operating margin of 2.5% means small cost or revenue swings can move profits sharply.
The Rangers spin-off expected on 2026-10-26 will change the company's structure and the comparability of its figures.
After 79.77% momentum, the strong trend score could reverse quickly if sentiment turns.
News ratings were reused from the 2026-10-14 run and not refreshed this run.
what_would_change: A rise of 10 points in the composite score to 65 would move the rating to Buy, most plausibly from a lower valuation or better margins lifting quality from 46.
A drop of 11 points to below 45 would move it to Sell, for example if the trend score (81) or growth score (85) fell back sharply.
Post-spin-off financials that change revenue growth, margins or multiples could shift several factors at once.
Negative news on guidance, analyst actions or the spin-off would pull the neutral news risk score (50) down.
